title: Historical Multimedia Project
subtitle: Facts, script, media, edit — and why that order.
objectives: Order the stages of a multimedia project
Explain why the script comes before the media
Explain what makes a historical project accurate

cards.title: The project fails in the planning
cards.text: A historical video goes wrong before a single clip is cut. The order you do things in decides whether it works.

cards.title: Four stages, in one order
cards.text: Each stage produces what the next one needs.
points: **Facts** — what happened, from sources you can name.
**Script** — what gets said, and in what order.
**Media** — the images and clips the script calls for.
**Edit and cite** — assemble it, credit everything.

cards.title: You plan the project
cards.text: Pick the first stage. Each wrong order shows what it would cost.

question.text: Why does the script come before gathering media?
options: The script says exactly which media you need
question.explain: That is the script's second job.

cards.title: Four rules for a history project
cards.text: An inaccurate project is worse than no project.
points: **Two sources** for anything surprising.
**Name your source on screen** or at the end.
**Separate what is documented** from what is argued.
**Say when you do not know.** That is a finding too.

question.text: Something surprising in your research should be…
question.explain: One source is a claim; two is a finding.

cards.title: Nobody builds the level first
cards.text: Game studios storyboard and block out before anything is made properly.
points: **Grey boxes first**, to test the shape.
**Art goes on last**, when the shape works.
**Changing a grey box costs minutes.**
**Changing a finished level costs weeks.**

cards.title: The script is where the thinking happens
cards.text: If the script is vague, no amount of editing will save it.
points: **Write it as sentences**, not bullet points.
**Read it aloud and time it.** That is your real length.
**If you cannot say it, you cannot narrate it.**
**Cut it by a quarter.** It will be better.

cards.title: Measure, then cut
cards.text: The workshop rule holds for projects exactly.
points: **A wrong cut wastes the part.**
**A wrong plan wastes the week.**
**Both are fixed by checking before committing.**
**Edit last** means you cut once.

cards.title: What to remember
points: Facts, script, media, edit — in that order.
The script tells you which media to gather.
Two sources for anything surprising; name every source.
Say plainly when something is not known.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 10 MAPEH, Arts strand, and the practical week of the term. The interactive is the content: he orders the stages himself and each wrong order is answered with its real cost rather than a cross. Picking the music first is included because it is the actual failure mode of a school multimedia project — the facts get cut to fit a song. The accuracy card gives four rules that transfer to any research task, including the one most students never hear: saying plainly that something is not known is a finding. Three lenses all say the same thing from three directions: check before you commit.
discussion: Ask what each stage produces for the next one.
Ask why the music cannot come first.
Ask how many sources a surprising fact needs.
Ask him to read his script aloud and time it.
extension: Have him actually make a two-minute project on one Term 2 Social Studies week.
Have him cut his own script by a quarter and compare the two.
misconceptions: "Gather the clips first, then write." The script is the shopping list.
"One source is enough." Two for anything surprising.
"Admitting you do not know looks weak." It is a finding.
